decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun within 3 years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To prevent the accumulation of unimplemented planning permissions and to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) and to meet the requirements of Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 and to meet the requirements of The Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015.
Condition : 2 - The development shall be carried out in accordance with the reports, specifications and drawings detailed 2525_HP_102 Rev.A [received 19th March 2026], 2525_HP_103 Rev.A [received 19th March 2026], 2525_HP_104 Rev.A [received 19th March 2026], 2525_HP_101 Rev.B [received 1st April 2026], 2525_HP_105 Rev.B [received 7th April 2026], Arboricultural Impact Assessment and Method Statement CAS/2026/126 by Cantia Arboricultural Services dated March 2026 [received 7th April 2026]
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory standard of development and to allow the local planning authority to review any potential changes to the scheme. 
Condition : 3 - All external materials used (except for the proposed Crittall doors to be installed into the rear elevation of the ground-floor rear/side extension) in the construction of the development hereby approved shall match the type, texture, tone, colour, size and profile of those used on the existing building and shall be retained permanently. 

The bricks of the replacement boundary wall shall be built in either Flemish bond or English garden wall bond using lime mortar.

The bricks of the proposed single-storey rear/side extension shall match the existing house, should be built in a matching bond using lime mortar and the pointing should be flush and rag finished to give a traditional appearance.

Reason: In the interest of the appearance of the development and to safeguard visual amenity of the conservation area, in accordance with Council policies LP1, LP2 and LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 4 - Prior to the installation of the replacement fenestrations, detailed fenestration specification drawings of the existing and proposed fenestrations should be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The drawings should include measurements of the glazing bars and frames and note the opening configurations.

Reason: In the interest of the appearance of the development and to safeguard visual amenity of the conservation area, in accordance with Council policies LP1, LP2 and LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 5 - The roof area of the development hereby permitted shall not be used as a balcony, roof garden or similar amenity area and furthermore, no balustrades, railings or other means of enclosure or means of permanent access shall be erected on this area.
Reason: To control overlooking and safeguard the privacy of neighbours in accordance with Council policies LP1 and LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 6 - No development shall commence until tree protection measures, as shown on the approved Arboricultural Impact Assessment and Method Statement CAS/2026/126 by Cantia Arboricultural Services dated March 2026 [received 7th April 2026] have been installed. The tree protection measures shall be retained for the duration of construction works and no materials, plant, storage, excavation or access shall take place within the protected areas unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To protect retained trees during construction in accordance with Policy LP56
Condition : 7 - All excavation works within or adjacent to the Root Protection Areas of retained trees shall be carried out under Arboricultural supervision and in accordance with the approved Arboricultural Method Statement. Any roots over 25mm diameter shall not be cut without the agreement of the supervising Arboricultural consultant and, where necessary, the Local Planning Authority. A report must be provided to the planning authority with clear and precise photographs as evidence.

Reason: To safeguard the health and long term retention of trees in accordance with Policy LP56.
Condition : 8 - INFORMATIVE: In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive manner and the Council has, as far as practicable, sought solutions to problems arising in relation to dealing with the planning application. The Council has made available detailed advice in the form of its statutory policies in the Local Plan (2023) as well as offering a full pre-application advice service, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably. In addition, where appropriate, further guidance was offered to the applicant during the processing of the application.
description: Alterations including erection of mansard roof extension to main rear roof, extension above two-storey back addition, alterations to roof of existing entrance porch, erection of single-storey rear/side extension, demolition of front boundary wall and erection of replacement front boundary wall and installation of replacement windows to front elevation.
